newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil parties to dicuss civil service reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil parties to dicuss civil service reform bill.

text.p: Brazilian political leaders were due to meet Monday and Tuesday to discuss opposition in Congress to the government's civil service reform bill, scheduled for a first Chamber of Deputies vote Wednesday.
Congressional officials said a proposed ceiling on public sector pay and pensions, which would hit many lawmakers' pockets, remained the stumbling block.
The ceiling would limit the total pay and pensions of working and retired civil servants to a maximum of 10,800 reais ($10,188) a month.
The proposal is one of the most important points of the civil service reform bill, which seeks to help reduce public sector spending on payrolls.
But it would reduce the income of an estimated 140 of the lower house's 513 members, who enjoy generous pensions from previous public sector posts on top of their 8,000 reais monthly salaries.
An aide to Deputy Wellington Moreira Franco, who began drawing up the reform bill in August 1995, said he expected the government to settle for a compromise.

The most likely solution would be to allow lawmakers along with other working officials to keep at least one pension from a previous public sector post, even if it took them over the 10,800 reais ceiling, the aide said.
"Clearly, the saving (in terms of public sector spending on pay) won't be as big as we proposed, but that's politics," the aide said.
